nodes.summary: The equation $x_1 + 2x_2 - x_3 - 2x_4 = 0$, with coefficient vector $(1, 2, -1, -2)$, has a canceling partition.
nodes.title: A canceling partition for $x_1 + 2x_2 - x_3 - 2x_4 = 0$

nodes.summary: Let $a_1, \dots, a_k$ be integers, the coefficients of the linear equation $a_1x_1 + \cdots + a_kx_k = 0$. The equation has a canceling partition when its indices split into pairs of distinct indices $i, j$ with $a_i + a_j = 0$; precisely, when there is a permutation $\sigma$ of the indices $1, \dots, k$ such that for every $i$ we have $\sigma(\sigma(i)) = i$, $\sigma(i) \ne i$ and $a_i + a_{\sigma(i)} = 0$.
nodes.title: Canceling partition

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a nontrivial finite abelian group, let $m \ge 1$, and let $a_1, \dots, a_{2m+1}$ be integers each coprime to the order $|G|$. Then for every $r \ge 3$ the equation $a_1x_1 + \cdots + a_{2m+1}x_{2m+1} = 0$ is $r$-uncommon over $G$.
nodes.title: Uncommonness of odd-length equations over finite abelian groups

nodes.title: Uncommon equations over a finite abelian group

nodes.summary: Let $m \ge 2$ and let $a_1, \dots, a_{2m}$ be nonzero integers, at least one negative and at least one positive, such that the equation $a_1x_1 + \cdots + a_{2m}x_{2m} = 0$ has no canceling partition. Then this equation is $r$-uncommon over the integers for every $r \ge 2$.
nodes.title: Uncommonness of even-length equations without a canceling partition

nodes.summary: Let $m \ge 1$ and let $a_1, \dots, a_{2m+1}$ be nonzero integers, at least one negative and at least one positive. Then for every $r \ge 3$ the equation $a_1x_1 + \cdots + a_{2m+1}x_{2m+1} = 0$ is $r$-uncommon over the integers.
nodes.title: Uncommonness of odd-length equations over the integers

nodes.summary: Let $k \ge 3$ and let $a_1, \dots, a_k$ be nonzero integers. If the equation $a_1x_1 + \cdots + a_kx_k = 0$ is $2$-uncommon over the integers, then it is $r$-uncommon over the integers for every $r \ge 3$.
nodes.title: Two-colour uncommonness over the integers extends to more colours

nodes.summary: For every $r \ge 2$, the equation $x + 2y - z - 2w = 0$ is $r$-uncommon over the integers.
nodes.title: Uncommonness of $x + 2y - z - 2w = 0$ over the integers

nodes.summary: The equation $x_1 + x_2 = 0$, with coefficient vector $(1, 1)$, has no canceling partition.
nodes.title: The equation $x_1 + x_2 = 0$ has no canceling partition

nodes.summary: For every finite abelian group $G$, every $k \ge 0$ and all integers $a_1, \dots, a_k$, the equation $a_1 x_1 + \dots + a_k x_k = 0$ is not $1$-uncommon over $G$.
nodes.title: No equation is 1-uncommon over a finite abelian group

nodes.summary: For every $k \ge 0$ and all integers $a_1, \dots, a_k$, the equation $a_1 x_1 + \dots + a_k x_k = 0$ is not $1$-uncommon over the integers.
nodes.title: No equation is 1-uncommon over the integers

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
